title: Review: Concentration–time graphs, half-life and clock reactions; Rate-determining step and mechanisms; Enthalpy change, exo/endothermic and profiles; Arrhenius equation
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EN01#t4 term and clue written for the game; EN01#t2 term and clue written for the game; KN05#t4 term and clue written for the game; EN01#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EN01#N.13, KN05#N.8b, KN06#N.5, KN07#N.4, EN01#N.7b, KN05#N.12a, KN06#N.13, KN07#N.13b, EN01#N.4b, KN06#N.3b, KN07#N.3, KN06#N.8. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Activation energy
items.clue: The minimum needed for reaction: from the reactant level to the top of the hump.

items.label: Surroundings
items.clue: Everything other than the reacting chemicals: water, container, thermometer, air.

items.label: Second order
items.clue: Rate against concentration curves upward ever more steeply; each halving takes longer.

items.label: Exothermic
items.clue: Describes a change in which the temperature around the chemicals rises; ΔH is negative.

questions.stem: Hydrated barium hydroxide and ammonium chloride, both solids, are mixed in a flask standing on a wet wooden block. Within a minute the water under the flask freezes, sticking the flask to the block. Which statement about the reacting chemicals is correct?

options.text: They lose energy to the water, which then freezes; ΔH is negative.
They release "cold", which spreads into the water and freezes it; ΔH is positive.
Energy is used up as the solids react, so the water freezes; ΔH is negative.
They gain energy from the water, flask and air; ΔH is positive.

questions.explanation: The surroundings cool because energy flows into the system. The system gains energy: endothermic, ΔH positive.

questions.stem: A hypothetical compound, A, decomposes in a reaction that is first order with respect to A. At a certain temperature the rate constant is k = 0.020 s⁻¹. In one trial at this temperature the initial concentration of A is 0.80 M. What is [A] after 25 s?

The reaction 2 NO(g) + O₂(g) → 2 NO₂(g) has the experimentally determined rate law rate = k[NO]²[O₂]. A student claims that this rate law shows that the reaction occurs in a single elementary step. Which evaluation of the claim is best?

options.text: Doubtful: a single step would need a rare collision of three particles at once.
Justified: orders equal to the coefficients show that a reaction is a single step.
Justified: a balanced equation shows the particles that collide in the reaction.
Doubtful: two molecules of one substance, NO, do not react in the same step.

questions.explanation: One step would fit the rate law, but it does not prove it. It would need three particles to collide at once, which is rare.

questions.stem: At a fixed temperature, a catalyst is added that lowers the activation energy of a reaction. What happens to the rate constant, k?

options.text: k is unchanged, as k depends only on temperature.
k increases, as more collisions now reach the lower activation energy.
k increases, as the catalyst makes the particles collide more often.
k increases, as the catalyst gives the particles more kinetic energy.

questions.explanation: Same energy distribution, lower threshold: more collisions succeed, so k rises.

questions.stem: Zinc metal reacts with hydrochloric acid in a flask connected to a gas syringe: Zn(s) + 2 HCl(aq) → ZnCl₂(aq) + H₂(g). As the reaction occurs, the solution becomes warmer and the H₂(g) pushes the syringe plunger outward. Taking the reacting species as the system, which statement correctly describes the energy changes?

options.text: The system gains energy, as shown by the rise in temperature of the solution
The system loses energy, which the reaction uses up instead of passing it to the surroundings
The system loses energy; the surroundings gain it as heat and as work on the plunger
The system loses energy only as heat; pushing the plunger out does not transfer energy

questions.stem: A hypothetical compound X decomposes at constant temperature. Results: t = 0, 200, 400, 600 s; [X] = 0.640, 0.320, 0.160, 0.080 M. A new trial at the same temperature starts at [X] = 0.320 M. How long does [X] take to fall to 0.080 M?
questions.explanation: [X] halves every 200 s, whatever the start: first order. 0.320 → 0.160 → 0.080 is two halvings: 400 s.

questions.stem: A hypothetical reaction occurs by a three-step mechanism. Relative to the reactants, the energies of the species along the reaction coordinate are: first transition state, +30 kJ/mol; first intermediate, +20 kJ/mol; second transition state, +105 kJ/mol; second intermediate, −10 kJ/mol; third transition state, +40 kJ/mol; products, −70 kJ/mol. Which step is the rate-determining step, and why?

options.text: Step 1, because the first step of a mechanism sets the rate of the reaction
Step 2, because its activation energy is the largest of the three steps
Step 1, because its products are higher in energy than its reactants
Step 3, because it has the largest energy change of the three steps

questions.stem: Two hypothetical elementary reactions, X and Y, have equal rates at 300 K. The activation energy of reaction X is 50 kJ/mol and that of reaction Y is 100 kJ/mol. Both reaction mixtures are heated to 310 K with no change in concentrations. Which statement about the rates at 310 K is correct?

options.text: The rate of Y rises by a greater factor than the rate of X does.
The rate of X goes up by a greater factor than the rate of Y does.
Each rate doubles, because each mixture is 10 K warmer than it was.
Each rate rises by the same small factor, as collisions become more frequent.

questions.explanation: The larger Ea, the more steeply the fraction of successful collisions rises with T. Y speeds up more.

questions.stem: A hot piece of copper is placed in cool water in an insulated cup, and the water becomes warmer. Which statement best describes, at the particulate level, how the water is warmed?

options.text: Heat, a substance held between the copper atoms, flows out of the metal and spreads among the water molecules
Cold leaves the water molecules and passes into the copper, so the water molecules are left warmer than before
Copper atoms collide with water molecules, which leave the collisions with more kinetic energy on average
Copper atoms pass on their high temperature to the water molecules, so each molecule becomes hot in itself

questions.stem: The decomposition of hydrogen peroxide in the presence of iodide ions is proposed to occur by the following mechanism. Step 1: H₂O₂(aq) + I⁻(aq) → H₂O(l) + IO⁻(aq). Step 2: H₂O₂(aq) + IO⁻(aq) → H₂O(l) + O₂(g) + I⁻(aq). Which statement correctly identifies the roles of I⁻ and IO⁻ in this mechanism?

options.text: I⁻ acts as a catalyst, and IO⁻ is an intermediate.
IO⁻ is a catalyst, and I⁻ is an intermediate.
I⁻ and IO⁻ are both intermediates in the steps.
I⁻ and IO⁻ both act as catalysts in the steps.

questions.explanation: I⁻ is used in step 1 and re-formed in step 2: catalyst. IO⁻ is formed in step 1 and used in step 2: intermediate.

questions.stem: For a reaction with Ea = 50 kJ/mol, raising the temperature from 300 K to 310 K almost doubles the rate. Which statement gives the main reason for this large increase?

options.text: A much larger fraction of all the collisions now have energy equal to or greater than Ea.
The particles move faster, so they collide more often, and more collisions give more reactions.
The activation energy decreases as the temperature rises, so more of the collisions succeed.
Every particle gains the same amount of energy, which carries many more of them past Ea.

questions.stem: The overall equation for a reaction is 2X + Y → X₂Y. The experimental rate equation is rate = k[X][Y]. Which mechanism is consistent with both?

options.text: Step 1: X + Y → XY (slow). Step 2: XY + X → X₂Y (fast).
Step 1: X + X → X₂ (slow). Step 2: X₂ + Y → X₂Y (fast).
Step 1: X + Y ⇌ XY (fast). Step 2: XY + X → X₂Y (slow).
Step 1: X + Y → XY (slow). Step 2: XY + Y → XY₂ (fast).

questions.explanation: The steps add to 2X + Y → X₂Y, and the slow first step has one X and one Y: rate = k[X][Y].
